title: Information Architecture Without Jargon
intro: Audit, sort, decide, test. Card sorts give ideas; tree tests give answers.

learn.title: In order
learn.text:
**Audit** how it works today → **card sort** to learn how people group things → **decide** the structure → **tree test** it.

Card sorting generates; tree testing evaluates.

try.q: What does a tree test do?
options: Checks people can find things in a structure
Shows how people would group content
Lists every page that exists today
try.explain: It evaluates a proposed or existing tree.

learn.title: Card sorting
learn.text:
**Open sort:** people make and name groups. The default.
**Closed:** your categories (a tree test is usually better).
**15+** people for qualitative, **30–50** for quantitative. **30–50 cards.**

try.q: How many cards should a sort have?
try.explain: More and people tire and dump the rest.

learn.title: Tree test metrics
learn.text:
**Success:** reached a correct place.
**Directness:** without backtracking.
**First click:** where they expected it.
**Destination:** where they ended up.

try.q: Clicks spread across several first options suggest:
try.explain: The item could belong in several places.

learn.title: Benchmarks
learn.text:
Across 98 studies the median task success was **62%**.
Below 40% poor · 61–80% good · above 90% excellent.
**Critical tasks: above 90%.** Comparing trees: about **50 people per tree**.

options: Not good enough for a critical task
try.explain: Critical and revenue tasks should pass 90%.

test.q: How does a structural audit ID a page two levels down?
test.explain: The ID shows its place in the hierarchy.

options: They take too long to run
test.explain: Use them only when sure of one or two categories.

test.q: Menu labels often differ from page titles. What does it suggest?
options: Inconsistent publishing or a broken back end

test.explain: Confident wrong turns are the worst failures.

test.q: Why may real-world findability beat a tree test?
options: The test removes search and visual cues

test.explain: Agree the words before the boxes.
